cues.say: Component 2: Load balancer. Sits in front of two or more identical copies of your backend, hands each request to one, and skips any copy that stops answering. You'll bring this up during version one, when you draw the basic design.
Think of it as: A traffic cop sending cars to open lanes. Use it for every design, and surviving a crashed copy.
Here's a real scenario. A tire shop's booking site runs 2 copies. At 9 AM, one crashes on a bug.
Without it: Only one copy: the site is down.
Every customer sees errors until someone restarts it.
With it: Health check gets no answer within seconds.
All traffic goes to the healthy copy.
Restarted copy passes the check and rejoins.
Why it works: One crash shouldn't take the whole site down.
In the interview, say: Two copies behind a load balancer, so one can die.
A few related terms you may hear.
Health check: The are you alive? ping, every few seconds.
HTTPS: Encryption usually ends at the load balancer.
Reverse proxy: Same idea: a server in front that forwards requests.
